cse404-java/u1.round2:
DEF | 1 | Object-Oriented Programming is a methodology or paradigm to design a program using classes and objects [1, 2].
MECH | 1 | Programs are organized into objects combining data and code that communicate with each other through message passing [2, 3].
SPEC | 1 | The book lists seven basic concepts: Object, Class, Data abstraction, Data encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Dynamic binding [2].
STEP | 1 | Conceptualize BankAccount as an object combining state like balance and behavior like deposit and withdrawal operations.
THIN | 1 | no
DEF | 2 | History of Java describes the creation and evolution of the language initiated by James Gosling and the Green Team at Sun Microsystems in 1991 [4, 5].
MECH | 2 | Java source code is compiled into platform-independent bytecode that is dynamically verified and executed by the Java Virtual Machine [6].
SPEC | 2 | Java was initially named Oak before being renamed Java in 1995 when incorporated by Netscape [7, 8].
STEP | 2 | Note that the BankAccount class source file compiles into bytecode executable across different operating system JVMs.
THIN | 2 | no
DEF | 3 | Data types represent the different values to be stored in a variable [9, 10].
MECH | 3 | Primitive data types directly store raw values in memory, whereas non-primitive data types store references to objects [9, 11].
SPEC | 3 | Java defines eight primitive data types: boolean (1 bit), byte (1 byte), char (2 bytes), short (2 bytes), int (4 bytes), long (8 bytes), float (4 bytes), and double (8 bytes) [9, 12, 13].
STEP | 3 | Choose double for the balance field and int for the account ID field of BankAccount.
THIN | 3 | no
DEF | 4 | A variable is a name of a memory location used to hold data of a declared type during program execution [14, 15].
MECH | 4 | Declaring a variable allocates memory according to its type, assigning default zero or false values to primitives and null to reference objects [11, 15].
SPEC | 4 | Java classifies variables into three types: local variable, instance variable, and static variable [14, 15].
STEP | 4 | Declare instance variables balance and accountNumber alongside a static variable accountCount inside BankAccount.
THIN | 4 | no
DEF | 5 | A constant is a variable whose value cannot be changed after declaration during program execution [12, 16].
MECH | 5 | Java uses the final keyword to lock variable assignment, causing any attempt to reassign the value to generate a compile-time error [12, 17].
SPEC | 5 | The syntax form within a class is modifier static final dataType variableName = value [14, 17].
STEP | 5 | Declare a private static final constant MINIMUM_BALANCE in BankAccount to enforce an unalterable minimum balance floor.
THIN | 5 | no
DEF | 6 | Comments are statements that are not executed by the compiler and interpreter, written to provide information or explanations to human readers [18-20].
MECH | 6 | The compiler ignores single-line and multi-line comments, while the javadoc tool extracts documentation comments to generate HTML API documentation [9, 19-21].
SPEC | 6 | Java provides three comment types: Single Line Comment (//), Multi Line Comment (/* */), and Documentation Comment (/** */) [19, 21, 22].
STEP | 6 | Add documentation comments above the BankAccount class definition and its constructors to document their functionality.
THIN | 6 | no
DEF | 7 | Operators are special symbols used in expressions to perform operations on operands [23-25].
MECH | 7 | Binary operators compute values from operands, and compound assignment operators evaluate expressions before storing results directly back into the variable [24].
SPEC | 7 | Shorthand assignment operators include +=, -=, *=, /=, and %= [24].
STEP | 7 | Apply the += shorthand operator inside a deposit method to add incoming funds directly to the balance field.
THIN | 7 | no
DEF | 8 | Type conversion and casting convert a value from one compatible or incompatible data type to another [26-28].
MECH | 8 | Widening conversion automatically promotes smaller compatible types to larger destination types, whereas narrowing requires explicit casting syntax for incompatible or larger-to-smaller assignments [26-28].
SPEC | 8 | The automatic widening hierarchy is byte -> short -> int -> long -> float -> double [29].
STEP | 8 | Explicitly cast a floating-point interest calculation to double when adding earned interest to the account balance.
THIN | 8 | no
DEF | 9 | Control structures direct the execution flow of a program through selection decisions and iterative loops [30, 31].
MECH | 9 | Conditional statements evaluate boolean expressions to branch execution, while loop statements repeat execution until a controlling condition becomes false [30].
SPEC | 9 | The jump statements break and continue exit a loop entirely or skip immediately to its next iteration [32, 33].
STEP | 9 | Implement an if conditional statement in a withdraw method to confirm the balance exceeds the requested withdrawal amount.
THIN | 9 | no
DEF | 10 | A class is a logical template or blueprint from which object instances sharing common properties and behaviors are created [34-36].
MECH | 10 | Memory for a class instance is dynamically allocated using the new operator, and instance members are accessed using the dot operator on object references [37, 38].
SPEC | 10 | General class declaration syntax uses the class keyword followed by the class name and a curly-brace delimited class body containing variable and method declarations [39].
STEP | 10 | Define the BankAccount class block, instantiate an object using new BankAccount(), and access its members via the dot operator.
THIN | 10 | no
DEF | 11 | Method overloading is the capability of defining multiple methods within the same class that share the same name but different parameter lists [40].
MECH | 11 | The Java compiler resolves overloaded method calls by matching the number, types, and sequence of argument values provided in the call [40].
SPEC | 11 | Overloaded methods must differ in their parameter signatures; differing solely by return type is invalid [40].
STEP | 11 | Overload the deposit method to accept either a single double amount or both a double amount and a String description parameter.
THIN | 11 | no
DEF | 12 | A constructor is a special member method used to initialize newly created objects of a class upon instantiation [41, 42].
MECH | 12 | A constructor shares the exact class name, has no return type, and executes automatically when an object is instantiated via the new operator [41, 42].
SPEC | 12 | Java supports default constructors with no arguments, parameterized constructors, and constructor overloading [41, 42].
STEP | 12 | Provide a default constructor initializing balance to zero and an overloaded parameterized constructor accepting an initial deposit, using this to disambiguate parameters from instance variables.
THIN | 12 | no
DEF | 13 | String handling encompasses creating and manipulating character sequences using String, StringBuffer, and StringBuilder classes [43, 44].
MECH | 13 | String instances store immutable character sequences in memory, whereas StringBuffer and StringBuilder objects provide mutable sequences that can be modified dynamically [43-45].
SPEC | 13 | The String class provides methods like charAt(), concat(), equals(), length(), and substring() [44, 46].
STEP | 13 | Use StringBuilder within an accountSummary method to build and return a formatted String representation of the BankAccount state.
THIN | 13 | no
cse404-java/u1.round3:
TOTAL | 720
SECTION | 1 | Object-Oriented Programming : | 70
POINT | 1 | Object-Oriented Programming organizes software around objects combining data and behavior rather than procedures acting on global data.
POINT | 1 | Encapsulation wraps state and methods into a single unit, hiding private implementation details from external functions.
POINT | 1 | Inheritance allows subclasses to reuse and extend superclass code, while polymorphism enables different object types to respond to uniform method calls.
SPEC | 1 | Object, Class, Data abstraction, Data encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Dynamic binding
STEP | 1 | Conceptualize BankAccount as an object encapsulating balance and account number state with deposit and withdrawal behaviors.
SECTION | 2 | History of Java | 35
POINT | 2 | Java was initiated by James Gosling and the Green Team at Sun Microsystems in 1991 for digital consumer devices.
POINT | 2 | Originally named Oak, it was renamed Java in 1995 and integrated into Netscape Navigator for internet programming.
POINT | 2 | Java source code compiles into platform-independent bytecode executed by the Java Virtual Machine.
SPEC | 2 | JDK 1.0 released January 23, 1996
STEP | 2 | Note that the BankAccount class compiles into bytecode executable on any platform JVM.
SECTION | 3 | Data types: | 50
POINT | 3 | Data types specify the size and type of values that can be stored in memory locations.
POINT | 3 | Java strictly distinguishes primitive types storing raw values from reference types storing memory addresses of objects.
POINT | 3 | Primitive integral types default to signed two's complement representations with fixed byte sizes.
SPEC | 3 | Eight primitives: boolean (1 bit), byte (1 byte), char (2 bytes), short (2 bytes), int (4 bytes), long (8 bytes), float (4 bytes), double (8 bytes)
STEP | 3 | Select double for storing balance and int for storing accountNumber in BankAccount.
SECTION | 4 | Variables: | 55
POINT | 4 | A variable is a named storage location allocated in memory according to its declared data type.
POINT | 4 | Instance variables exist as long as their owning object exists, while local variables exist only during method execution.
POINT | 4 | Static variables belong to the class itself and are shared among all instances.
SPEC | 4 | Syntax: type identifier [ = value ];
STEP | 4 | Declare instance fields balance and accountNumber alongside a static field accountCount in BankAccount.
SECTION | 5 | Constant: | 30
POINT | 5 | Constants store fixed values that cannot be modified after initial assignment during execution.
POINT | 5 | The final modifier prevents variable reassignment and causes compile-time errors upon modification attempts.
POINT | 5 | Class-level constants combine static and final modifiers to create single shared immutable values.
SPEC | 5 | modifier static final dataType variableName = value
STEP | 5 | Declare a private static final constant MINIMUM_BALANCE in BankAccount.
SECTION | 6 | Comments: | 25
POINT | 6 | Comments are compiler-ignored annotations that document program functionality for developers.
POINT | 6 | Single-line comments start with double slashes, while multi-line comments are bounded by slash-asterisk delimiters.
POINT | 6 | Documentation comments are processed by the javadoc utility to generate external HTML API documentation.
SPEC | 6 | Three types: // single-line, /* multi-line */, /** javadoc */
STEP | 6 | Add javadoc comments documenting the BankAccount class and method behaviors.
SECTION | 7 | Operators: | 60
POINT | 7 | Operators perform specific mathematical, relational, logical, or bitwise operations on operands.
POINT | 7 | Operator precedence and associativity rules dictate the exact sequence in which unparenthesized expressions evaluate.
POINT | 7 | Compound assignment operators evaluate an expression and assign the result directly back to the target variable.
SPEC | 7 | Shorthand assignment operators: +=, -=, *=, /=, %=
STEP | 7 | Use the += compound operator in deposit to update the balance field.
SECTION | 8 | Type conversions and casting | 45
POINT | 8 | Type conversion alters a value from its original data type to another compatible or explicitly requested type.
POINT | 8 | Automatic widening conversion occurs when assigning a smaller compatible type to a larger destination type.
POINT | 8 | Explicit narrowing casting is mandatory when assigning larger types to smaller types to acknowledge potential precision loss.
SPEC | 8 | Widening order: byte -> short -> int -> long -> float -> double
STEP | 8 | Explicitly cast a floating-point interest calculation to double before updating BankAccount balance.
SECTION | 9 | Control Structure: | 70
POINT | 9 | Control structures govern program execution flow through conditional branching and iterative loops.
POINT | 9 | Selection statements evaluate boolean conditions to branch execution along alternative code paths.
POINT | 9 | Iteration loops repeat statement blocks until a controlling termination condition evaluates to false.
POINT | 9 | Jump statements break and continue immediately exit loops or skip to the next iteration.
SPEC | 9 | Control constructs: if-else, switch, while, do-while, for, break, continue
STEP | 9 | Use an if condition in withdraw to verify sufficient balance before deducting funds.
SECTION | 10 | CLASSES | 100
POINT | 10 | A class defines a user-defined template specifying instance fields and instance methods for object creation.
POINT | 10 | Object instantiation allocates memory dynamically on the heap via the new operator and returns a reference.
POINT | 10 | Access modifiers control member visibility across class, package, and subclass boundaries.
POINT | 10 | The this reference resolves namespace collisions between instance variables and local parameter names.
SPEC | 10 | Access specifiers: public, private, protected, default (package-private)
STEP | 10 | Define class BankAccount with private balance, public methods, and use this to disambiguate field assignments.
SECTION | 11 | Method Overloading | 50
POINT | 11 | Method overloading permits multiple methods within the same class to share an identical name.
POINT | 11 | Overloaded methods must possess distinct parameter lists differing in parameter count, types, or order.
POINT | 11 | The compiler selects the appropriate overloaded method at compile time based on invocation argument types.
SPEC | 11 | Method signature rule: parameter list must differ; return type alone cannot differentiate methods.
STEP | 11 | Overload deposit to accept either a single double amount or a double amount with a String description.
SECTION | 12 | Constructors | 75
POINT | 12 | Constructors are special class members invoked automatically during object allocation to initialize state.
POINT | 12 | A constructor has no return type and must share the exact name of its enclosing class.
POINT | 12 | Classes support default zero-argument constructors, parameterized constructors, and constructor overloading.
SPEC | 12 | Constructor syntax: [access_modifier] ClassName(parameter_list) { body }
STEP | 12 | Provide a default constructor setting balance to zero and a parameterized constructor taking an initial deposit.
SECTION | 13 | String handling | 55
POINT | 13 | Strings in Java represent sequences of characters managed via dedicated standard library classes.
POINT | 13 | String object instances are immutable, meaning string modifications create new objects rather than altering existing instances.
POINT | 13 | StringBuffer and StringBuilder classes provide mutable character sequences for efficient string construction.
SPEC | 13 | String methods: charAt(), concat(), equals(), length(), substring()
STEP | 13 | Use StringBuilder in an accountSummary method to construct a string representation of BankAccount.
